title: Politeness, requests & invitations
goal: Make polite requests, ask permission, invite and be invited, and accept or refuse gracefully.
intro:
Urdu is famous across South Asia for its **تہذیب** (tehzīb) — refined manners — and its polite speech. Beyond آپ and جی, there is a whole layer of honorific verbs: guests don't just 'come', they **تشریف لاتے ہیں** ('bring their honour'); elders don't just 'say', they **فرماتے ہیں**.

This unit covers the extra-polite imperative (**کیجیے گا**), the **subjunctive** for 'shall I…? / let's… / may…', and the art of offering, accepting and refusing.

grammar.title: Polite imperatives and requests
grammar.body:
From least to most polite:

**کرو** (تم form) → **کریں** → **کیجیے** → **کیجیے گا** (polite imperative + گا: the 'future imperative', extra courteous, or for something to be done later: آتے رہیے گا 'do keep visiting').

Requests are softened with **ذرا** 'just', **مہربانی کر کے** / **پلیز** 'please', and the compound helper **دینا** (doing something *for* someone): دروازہ کھول دیجیے 'please open the door (for me)'.

The politest request is a question with **سکنا**: کیا آپ … کر سکتے ہیں؟ 'could you…?'. Even softer: کیا آپ … کر دیں گے؟ 'would you…?'.

Honorific verbs replace ordinary ones when speaking to or about respected people: آنا → **تشریف لانا**, بیٹھنا → **تشریف رکھنا**, کہنا → **فرمانا**. Never use them about yourself!

grammar.title: The subjunctive: 'shall I…?', 'let's…', 'may…'
grammar.body:
The subjunctive is the future tense **without گا**: میں کروں، تو/وہ کرے، ہم/آپ/وہ کریں، تم کرو. It expresses possibility, suggestions and wishes:

**Shall I…?** کیا میں چائے بناؤں؟ 'Shall I make tea?'
**Let's…** چلیں! 'Let's go!', بیٹھیں؟ 'Shall we sit?'
**Wishes and blessings:** اللہ آپ کو خوش رکھے 'May God keep you happy', آپ کی عمر لمبی ہو 'May you live long'.
**After 'want someone to', 'it's better that', 'maybe':** میں چاہتا ہوں کہ آپ آئیں 'I want you to come'; شاید وہ آئے 'maybe he'll come'.

examples.en: May God keep you happy. (a common thank-you)

examples.en: I'd like you to eat with us.

examples.en: It's better that we leave early.

dialogue.title: A dinner invitation
dialogue.setting: James arrives at his colleague Mr Siddiqui's home for dinner.

lines.en: How can that be? You'll have to have some tea!

lines.en: Dinner is served. Come, please help yourself.

lines.en: Everything is delicious. You've gone to so much trouble.

lines.speaker: Mrs Siddiqui
lines.native: کوئی زحمت نہیں۔ تھوڑی اور بریانی لیجیے!
lines.roman: ko’ī zahmat nahīṃ. thoṛī aur biryānī lījiye!
lines.en: No trouble at all. Have a little more biryani!

lines.speaker: James
lines.native: بس، شکریہ۔ اب مجھے اجازت دیجیے۔ اللہ آپ کو خوش رکھے۔
lines.roman: bas, shukriya. ab mujhe ijāzat dījiye. allāh āp ko xush rakhe.
lines.en: That's enough, thank you. I must take my leave now. God bless you.

culture: Hospitality (مہمان نوازی) is a sacred duty: a guest is said to be a blessing from God. Expect to be offered food and drink repeatedly; the ritual of polite refusal and host insistence (اصرار) is part of the etiquette, so if you really don't want more, refuse firmly with a hand on your chest. Bringing sweets (مٹھائی) or fruit when visiting is customary. Leave-taking is lengthy — 'ijāzat dījiye' signals you're about to go, and the host will usually urge you to stay a little longer.

lessons.title: Excuse me, could you help?

tip.title: Could you…? ذرا, دیجیے, سکتے ہیں
tip.body:
- Soften a request with **ذرا** 'just' or **مہربانی کر کے** 'please': ذرا سنیے 'excuse me'.
- Add **دینا** for a favour done for you: کھڑکی کھول **دیجیے** 'open the window for me, please'.
- Politest of all, a question with **سکنا**: کیا آپ … **کر سکتے** ہیں؟ 'could you…?'

lessons.title: Welcoming a guest

tip.title: Words of honour: تشریف لائیے
tip.body:
- For respected people, everyday verbs get grander: آنا → **تشریف لانا**, بیٹھنا → **تشریف رکھنا**, کہنا → **فرمانا**.
- **تشریف لائیے** 'please come in', **تشریف رکھیے** 'please sit', **فرمائیے** 'how can I help?'.
- Never use them about yourself: say میں **آیا**, not میں تشریف لایا.

lessons.title: Shall I make tea?

tip.title: Shall I…? کیا میں چائے بناؤں؟
tip.body:
- The subjunctive is the future **without گا**: میں **بناؤں**, ہم **بیٹھیں**, آپ **لیں**.
- Offers: کیا میں چائے **بناؤں**؟ 'shall I make tea?' · Suggestions: **چلیں**؟ 'shall we go?'
- Wishes too: اللہ آپ کو صحت **دے** 'may God give you health'.
- Hosts insist: **تکلف نہ کریں** 'don't be shy, help yourself'.

lessons.title: Accepting and turning down invitations

tip.title: Yes and no to an invitation
tip.body:
- Accept warmly: **ضرور!** or **بڑی خوشی سے** 'with great pleasure'.
- Refuse gently: **معذرت**, then: میں نہیں آ **سکوں گا / گی** 'I won't be able to come'.
- Hosts will **insist** (اصرار) — a polite first 'no' is expected, so say no twice if you mean it.

tip.title: Blessings: اللہ آپ کو خوش رکھے
tip.body:
- Wishes use the subjunctive (no گا): اللہ آپ کو خوش **رکھے** 'may God keep you happy' — a warm way to say thank you.
- **مبارک ہو!** 'congratulations!' — the reply is **خیر مبارک**.
- Leaving: **اب مجھے اجازت دیجیے** 'I must take my leave now'.
